messages:
Sam: Heads-up 10: we need final decisions for partner tiers + MDF allocation before Friday so QBR deck can include the updated numbers. Quick sync?
Priya: I'm available. Main questions: do we keep per-deal caps for SI integrations, and how to treat co-marketing vs. co-engineering credits?
Diego: Proposal: split MDF into two pools  Marketplace onboarding (HW/software SKU verification) and SI enablement (training + joint PoCs). Different release rules.
Olivia: For marketplace onboarding let's require listing + verified SKU tests. Release 50% on listing, 50% on first paid customer. This avoids credits used as pure discounts.
Hannah: Finance note: we'll need to model cashflow if we front 75% for fast-track partners. Use FinanceBot to snapshot current MDF commitments.
FinanceBot: Snapshot generated: total_mdf_pool=1,200,000; committed=420,000; available=780,000 (as of 2026-03-15 09:31 UTC). Report link: https://finance.redwood.example/mdf-snapshots/1865001234

Sam: Good. Diego, can you sketch a simple tier table? Something like Tier A (Strategic): high MDF, co-selling, announcement; Tier B: smaller MDF, enablement only; Tier C: self-serve listing support.
Diego: Drafting now. Thinking fields: tier_name, typical_commitment, expected_pipeline_quota, MDF_ceiling, deliverables
Priya: Also add a 'announcement cadence' column. For joint announcements we should hold press/marketplace listing dates until product PM signs off. Avoid surprise launches.
Olivia: For hardware partners (Nebula Systems + AtlasCloud pilot) we need SKU-level onboarding timelines. Suggested SLA: 4 weeks for validation if partner provides test images and infra. If Redwood needs to run tests, extend to 8 weeks.
Hannah: For MDF math, we should tie tranche releases to measurable milestones: 1) Listing published, 2) Joint webinar scheduled, 3) First paid customer. No tranche unless milestone verified.

Priya: Scoring rubric thought: pipeline_influence (0-10), go_to_market_readiness (0-10), technical_gap (0-10). Threshold for Tier A = 8+ weighted (weights: 50/30/20).
Sam: Agree. Add an override path for strategic logos (exec sign-off).

Diego: I'll add a 'clawback' clause to the playbook: if partner uses MDF to discount deals and we don't see uplift within 12 months, prorated recouping or reduced future eligibility. Legal to confirm language.
Priya: Also call out co-marketing credit vs. engineering credit in the sheet. They should be separate budget lines and tracked to different P&L tags.

Olivia: Quick operational ask: who owns marketplace listing QA? Suggest Eng-Platform does verification and signs off on SKU badge. @Sam can we ask them to prioritize up to 2 listings next sprint?
Sam: Yes, I'll raise with Eng-Platform.

Hannah: Action items: 
- Diego: publish tier table + scoring sheet (today)
- Priya: clarify co-marketing vs. co-engineering budget lines in sheet (today)
- Olivia: draft onboarding SLA for HW marketplace (tomorrow)
- Sam: escalate Eng-Platform QA capacity & request exec override template (tomorrow)
- FinanceBot: export MDF commitment report for QBR deck (EOD)

Priya: Can we run a short poll on fast-track criteria? If a partner has existing marketplace badges + 3 production customers, qualify for 75% upfront credits.
Diego: Poll: Fast-track criteria OK? :ballot_box_with_ballot:
Olivia: +1
Sam: +1 (but with legal clawback)
Hannah: +1 from finance side if we have clear milestones

FinanceBot: Poll closed: yes=4 no=0 abstain=0

Sam: Great. I'll assemble a single slide for QBR summarizing tiers, MDF buckets, and fast-path rules. Drop any supporting docs in the qbr folder: https://docs.redwood.example/qbr/partners/1865

Priya: Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll mark this as ready for review and loop Legal for clawback language.
Olivia: 👍 thanks.
FinanceBot: Reminder set: QBR deck deadline 2026-03-19 17:00 UTC (thread: 1865001234).
